title: Smooth local polarizations of proper flat curve families
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to T$ a morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] which is proper, flat and of finite presentation. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; flatness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts. Suppose that every geometric fibre $X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, has dimension at most one, with empty fibres allowed. Dimension is the supremum of the Krull dimensions of affine etale charts [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$. There exist a scheme $U$, a smooth surjective morphism $p:U\to T$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and an invertible module $L$ on the scheme $Y=X\times_TU$ [def-sc-invertible-module], such that $L|_{Y\times_UW}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] for every affine open $W\subseteq U$. Here $Y$ is a scheme representing the algebraic-space fibre product [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Surjective means that the image of $|U|$ is all of $|T|$. There is no Noetherian, connectedness, reducedness, nonempty-fibre or pure-dimension hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0DQ0 (lemma-polarized-curves-over-curves), smooth surjectivity of PolarizedCurves to Curves; its scheme-atlas consequence explicitly unwound in the first paragraph of the proof of Tag 0E6F (lemma-etale-locally-scheme). PolarizedCurves objects immediately before lemma-polarized-curves-in-polarized specify schemes and relatively ample invertible modules; section-stack-curves specifies the family hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-picard-stack-smooth] to $f$. Its geometric-fibre hypothesis is exactly the dimension hypothesis of the item, including empty fibres. Choose its smooth surjective scheme atlas $a:V\to\mathcal P_f$ with smooth composite $q:V\to T$. By the definition of this Picard stack, $a$ is a line module $M$ on the algebraic space $X_V=X\times_TV$, with cartesian pullbacks as specified in that node. At this point $X_V$ need not be a scheme.

By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], the base change $X_V\to V$ is proper. Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-ample-locus] to it and $M$. It gives an open subscheme $U\subset V$ characterized on every scheme test $B\to V$ by relative ampleness of $M_B$. In particular $Y=X_V\times_VU=X\times_TU$ is a scheme and $M_U$ corresponds to an ordinary invertible module $L$ on $Y$, ample over every affine open of $U$. This is exactly the scheme/ordinary-line convention in the statement of the ample-locus node. The composite $p:U\hookrightarrow V\xrightarrow{q}T$ is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. It remains to prove its surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0DQ0, openness of the ample locus by spaces-descent.tex Tag 0D3D (lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood); moduli-curves.tex Tag 0E6F (lemma-etale-locally-scheme), first paragraph.

proof.text: Fix any geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], $C=X_{\bar t}$ is proper over $\Omega$, hence separated and of finite type. Its dimension is at most one by hypothesis. Thus [lem-sfb-separated-space-dimension-one-scheme] makes $C$ a scheme. Apply [lem-sc-proper-dim-one-projective] to obtain a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_\Omega$. By [lem-pc-very-ample-ample], $A=i^*\mathcal O(1)$ is ample and remains ample after every field extension of $\Omega$. Regard $A$ as a line module on the small etale site of $C$ using [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. It is an object of $\mathcal P_f(\Omega)$. These results permit nonreduced, disconnected and zero-dimensional $C$, as well as $C=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0DQ0, surjectivity paragraph; spaces-over-fields.tex Tag 0ADD (lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus) and varieties.tex Tag 0A26 (lemma-dim-1-proper-projective).

proof.text: The surjectivity clause of [lem-sfb-space-picard-stack-smooth], applied to $A\in\mathcal P_f(\Omega)$, supplies a field extension $\Omega\hookrightarrow K$ and $v:\operatorname{Spec}K\to V$ over $T$ with $M_v\cong A_K$. By [lem-pc-very-ample-ample], $A_K$ is ample on the scheme $C_K$. The etale/ordinary-module comparison of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] respects pullback, so $M_v$ is relatively ample over $\operatorname{Spec}K$. The test-scheme characterization of [lem-sfb-space-relative-ample-locus] therefore makes $v$ factor through $U$. For each point $t\in T$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(t)$ and apply this construction to its geometric point. The unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ maps to a point of $U$ lying over $t$. Thus $|U|\to|T|$ is surjective. Together with step 2 this supplies $p,Y,L$ with every asserted property. If $T$ is empty the surjectivity assertion is vacuous and the same construction still applies.
